exclusion_reason: The pre-Win32 emulator lane exists as a header-signature boundary: DOS (plain MZ), Win16 (NE), and the LE/LX linear family are admitted to the emulator lane under a declared sandbox confinement contract that denies all host reach, while a Win32 PE32/PE32+ image is refused and kept on the binary lane. The benchmark stays red because no emulator core is embedded — admission never becomes execution — until the sandboxed core lands under the BPTK-002 corpus denominator.
promotion_trigger: Promote when pre-Win32 fixture route to the lane and the PE32 fixture never does.
expected_failing_assertion: No emulator core is embedded, so an admitted pre-Win32 input stays blocked and is never executed.
active_gate_evidence: test/emulator.test.mjs asserts DOS/Win16/LE admission with host-reach-denied sandbox, PE32 refusal onto the binary lane, the never-executed blocked terminal state, and reachability at the real CLI keeping PE32 out.
procedure: Route the DOS and Win16 fixture to the emulator lane.
Assert the PE32 fixture stays on its own lane.
Assert the emulator lane cannot reach host file system beyond the bundle.
pass_criterion: PE32 is never mis-routed and the lane stays confined.
